summary: Heinrich von Stietencron was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Munich, SOAS London, and Heidelberg. After serving as an assistant at Heidelberg in 1965, he held a chair at the University of Tübingen from 1973 to 1998.

Heinz Adolf Mode worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and archaeology. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin, under G. P. Malalasekera and Otto Fischer, and completed his Promotion and Habilitation at Basel. He was a professor at Halle-Wittenberg (1948–1978).

Heinz Bechert was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Munich, Hamburg, and Mainz under Ernst Waldschmidt and Erich Frauwallner. After assistant and Privatdozent posts at Saarland and Mainz, he served as Chair of Indology at Göttingen (1965–2000).

Helen Hardacre specializes in Japanology and religious studies. She studied at Vanderbilt and the University of Chicago under Joseph Kitagawa and Jonathan Z. Smith. She held posts at Princeton (1980–1989), Griffith (1990–1992), and Harvard University from 1992.

Helen Josephine Baroni is a scholar of Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She studied under Paul B. Watt at Columbia University and held a post at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (attested 2006).

Helen Wang specializes in Sinology, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at SOAS University of London from around 1984 to 1988 and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.
Helena Blankleder works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Taklung Tsetrul Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche (attested 1999).
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania between 1979 and 1984. She held a post at Rice University beginning around 1990.

Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. She completed her Ph.D. at the University of Munich (c. 1960–1967) and joined the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities as a scientific collaborator in 1964.

Hellfried Dahlmann was a linguist who taught Claus Vogel. He held academic posts at the University of Marburg from approximately 1941 to 1953 and at the University of Cologne from approximately 1953 to 1970.

Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm studied at Frankfurt, Kiel, Grenoble, and Berlin under Otto Franke. He served as assistant at Frankfurt, taught German at Peking University (1933–1948), and held the sinology chair at the University of Washington from 1948 to 1971.

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (1942–1948) and under Paul Debes in 1945. He served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from approximately 1952 to 1988.

Helmer Smith worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He studied at Uppsala and under Richard Pischel and Karl Friedrich Geldner. He served as Dozent at Lund (1921) and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Uppsala (1936–1947).

Helmut Eimer was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Berlin, Hamburg, and Bonn, completing his doctorate at Bonn under Frank-Richard Hamm, and held a post at the University of Bonn from around 1975 to 2001.

Helmut Hoffmann was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Freiburg, Berlin (under Heinrich Lüders), and Marburg, he held posts at the Prussian Academy, Munich (1948–1968), and Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied and completed his Habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at the University of Vienna and the Austrian Academy of Sciences, directing its Institute for Cultural and Intellectual History.

Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Würzburg, Heidelberg (PhD 1950), and Tübingen. He held posts at Neuendettelsau, Tübingen, the University of Regensburg, and served as professor at the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied under Ernst Steinkellner. He has held faculty posts at the University of Vienna (attested 1983–2026) and served as a Numata visiting professor at Leiden University.

Helmuth von Glasenapp was an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He studied at Tübingen, Munich, Berlin, and Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He held posts at Berlin, Bonn, and occupied chairs at Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).

Helwig Schmidt-Glintzer is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Göttingen (c. 1967–1969) and the University of Munich (c. 1969–1973), later holding posts at Munich (c. 1981–1993) and Göttingen (c. 1993–2015).
